lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Elizabeth opens with their private shorthand of understanding.

lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Flush's ecstatic reunion shows how vividly their life together is imagined.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: Robert admits he sometimes shortened visits just to reach the moment of taking her hand.

lines.text: How I wish for two hearts to love you with, and two lives to give to you, and two souls to bear the weight worthily of all you have given to me.
lines.note: Elizabeth's wish for two hearts and two lives is one of the letter's most intimate declarations.

lines.text: Is this absence contrived on purpose to prove how foolishly I said that I loved you the more from seeing you the oftener?
lines.note: Robert teases that absence seems designed to test his claim about loving her more.

lines.text: Chiappino little knew how right he was, when he used to taunt me with my ‘New Cross Knight.’
lines.note: Elizabeth revives the private 'New Cross Knight' taunt from Chiappino.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: The sudden loss of Flush brings one of the correspondence's most vivid domestic alarms.

lines.text: ‘Our friend and follower, that was to be’—is that, then, your opinion of my poor darling Flush’s destiny— Ah,—I should not have been so quiet if I had not known differently and better.
lines.note: Elizabeth answers Robert's 'friend and follower' phrase after Flush's rescue.

lines.text: ‘The milk,’ answers Ba, is exactly to correct the superabundant gall of bitterness which overflowed lately about Flush.
lines.note: Robert turns the milk-diet into a witty callback during the Flush dispute.

lines.text: And smiling to myself I was, both last night and this morning, at your phrase about the ‘business’ to be talked by the ‘grave man and woman’; understanding your precaution against all unlawful jesting!—jesters forbidden in the protocol!
lines.note: Elizabeth jokes that jesters are forbidden by their 'protocol,' echoing their grave-business talk.

lines.text: You have given me the highest, completest proof of love that ever one human being gave another.
lines.note: Robert calls her gift of herself the highest proof of love one person can give another.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: Elizabeth's 'oh, such a day!' captures the breathless aftermath of the wedding.

lines.text: Dearest, dearestest!—And you do not start at that word, ‘Irrevocable,’ as I have had fancies that you might, when the time came!’
lines.note: Elizabeth tests whether Robert will flinch at the word 'Irrevocable.'

lines.text: Is this my last letter to you, ever dearest?
lines.note: Her question about this being her last letter gives the farewell its final ache.
